_: The table declarations. This is data: the installer recognises none of the names below. docs/tables.md is the authority on the shape.

tables.name: handle
tables._: One row = one callable thing. The database holds only the name; the real function lives in the in-process registry. This row is what tells the kernel such a function exists.

columns.name: name
columns._: fn: runs inside the kernel process; http:// runs in another process

columns.name: expect_ms
columns._: How long it is expected to take; past this it is declared dead. Same rule inside and out

columns.name: module
columns._: Where an fn: implementation comes from: `path#exportName`. Empty = shipped with the binary (the ones registered in code). Out-of-process handles do not use this column

tables.name: api
tables._: A row is defined by which environment variable holds the key, plus the model to call. Secrets never enter the database.

columns.name: handle
columns._: → handle.name

columns.name: modes
columns._: Its values are registered in the mode table

columns.name: base_url
columns._: Where the calls go. In the table, not in the code: an address that lives only in code cannot be seen in a snapshot, and one that lives in an environment variable cannot be seen at all. Point a row somewhere else and that row goes somewhere else

columns.name: retry_on
columns._: Which failures are worth trying again, as a JSON list of HTTP status codes plus the word network for a call that never got a reply. Anything not listed is returned as it is - a 400 says the request itself was wrong, and sending it again only spends the clock to fail the same way. Which failures are transient differs per key and per model, so it lives on this row rather than in code

tables.name: cycle
tables._: The cycle table. One row = one cycle within one mode. This is what the kernel advances on.

columns.name: mode
columns._: 1 which mode

columns.name: cycle
columns._: 2 which cycle within that mode

columns.name: api_mode
columns._: Which api mode this cycle needs (chat / duplex / ...). Empty = this station uses no model and goes through agent.unit

columns.name: must_call
columns._: The one tool this station has to call. Empty = it picks for itself. Set, and the call goes out with that tool forced, so the station cannot end without it. Note that some vendors refuse a forced choice while their thinking mode is on

columns.name: max_units
columns._: 3 how many execution units are allowed

columns.name: from
columns._: 4 which rows it usually comes from. A JSON list

columns.name: next
columns._: 5 which rows usually come next. A JSON list

columns.name: infer
columns._: 6 the inference function -> handle.name. Columns 4 and 5 decide it

tables.name: task
tables._: The task table. One row = the head node of one task.

columns.name: mode
columns._: -> cycle.mode, which also decides which sub-table holds the detail

columns.name: place
columns._: → workplace.place

columns.name: run
columns._: What this run is called. One bench is a batch of tasks, identified by this. Empty = belongs to no run

columns.name: source
columns._: Who published it: user / agent / world / eacn. This is an admission criterion, not metadata

columns.name: domain
columns._: Which kind of problem this is (physics / chem / coding ...). Extensions are dispatched on it: a skill / tool / rule states its applicability as a dim=task,key=domain term. It does not belong in mode: mode is the reasoning mechanism (cot / tot / tree), which is a different axis from what field the problem is in. Empty = unclassified

columns.name: description
columns._: The task description in natural language. Transparent to the kernel; how to read it is the agent's business

columns.name: created_at
columns._: Wall-clock creation time; metadata

columns.name: workdir
columns._: The landing path inside that place. Empty = the cwd on that machine

columns.name: objective
columns._: Whether this task has a grading function. The definition is not here: it is in the sealed store, out of reach of the API

columns.name: readable
columns._: A policy bit: whether the definition of the grading function may be read directly. If a task carries one, this must be given explicitly; there is no default

columns.name: claimed_by
columns._: The current holder. Empty = unclaimed

columns.name: result
columns._: The wrap-up result. Only present once done or failed

columns.name: max_branches
columns._: How many branches may be open at once

columns.name: max_dead_siblings
columns._: How many dead siblings under one parent before backtracking a level to change direction

columns.name: solve_seconds
columns._: Upper bound on solving time, in seconds

columns.name: state
columns._: Where it stands: open / claimed / done / failed. Derived from the sub-table, then written back

tables.name: agent
tables._: One row = one agent (an agent card, unpacked).

columns.name: config
columns._: Where its config file is

columns.name: apis
columns._: A JSON list; each entry is [key_env, model]

columns.name: unit
columns._: The execution-unit handle -> handle.name

tables.name: workplace
tables._: Registers the places where work happens. Not a lookup table.

columns.name: place
columns._: A layered address string

columns.name: runtime
columns._: The runtime shipped over when the connection is made (a local file path). Empty for local

columns.name: forward
columns._: Whether tools are forwarded there

columns.name: tools
columns._: The allow-list. A JSON list; each entry carries a policy

columns.name: usable
columns._: Registered availability, not a liveness probe

tables.name: rule
tables._: Rules. They may be registered from outside, and rows appear at any time.

columns.name: identity
columns._: → handle.name

columns.name: params
columns._: JSON

columns.name: writes
columns._: Declares which tables it writes and how. JSON

columns.name: access
columns._: How an external rule reaches the database. JSON; secrets are stored only as environment variable names

columns.name: scope
columns._: Which rows it may touch. A structured match expression, not a SQL fragment

tables.name: trigger
tables._: When my turn comes. Shared by rule / skill / tool. One row = one term.

columns.name: group
columns._: AND within a group, OR across groups

columns.name: dim
columns._: agent / task / cycle / chain

columns.name: key
columns._: Empty string for the chain dimension

tables.name: tool
tables._: One row = one tool. name is what the model sees, and what the workplace allow-list references.

columns.name: identity
columns._: → handle.name

columns.name: does
columns._: The description the model reads

columns.name: params
columns._: The argument schema the model reads

columns.name: output
columns._: The result schema, also read by the model

columns.name: prompt
columns._: A usage convention this tool adds to the system instructions

columns.name: concurrent
columns._: Whether it may run alongside other tools

columns.name: system
columns._: A system tool: every agent has it from the start, with no trigger lookup

tables.name: skill
tables._: One row = one skill. The model does not pick it; it is injected when its terms match.

columns.name: identity
columns._: → handle.name

columns.name: body
columns._: Empty for dynamically generated ones; the handle produces the content on demand

tables.name: mcp_server
tables._: Registers one MCP server. Its tools are not written here: once connected it reports them through tools/list, and each grows one row in tool.

columns.name: name
columns._: Its name. Handle names are mcp:<name>/<tool>, so it must not contain a /

columns.name: spec
columns._: How to start it. JSON, the same shape as an MCP client config: {command,args,env} or {url,headers}. Secrets are stored only as environment variable names

tables.name: msg_role
tables._: Registers message roles, and where each one goes on the way out. This is the only place that says it: the same kind can wear two roles (the world injects one as user, the kernel injects one as system), so where a line goes cannot be read off its kind.

columns.name: sent_as
columns._: messages = a line in the conversation. instructions = part of what this turn is told, resent every turn and not a thing anyone said

tables.name: msg_kind
tables._: Registers message kinds. Adding one = adding a row; no other table changes.

templates._: Task sub-tables: one per mode present in the cycle table.

columns.name: node
columns._: Which tree node this unit belongs to. **Only a tree-shaped mechanism has nodes**: there a node is a whole attempt, several units stitched together and closed by the one that gets a terminal status. A single-chain mechanism has no attempts to tell apart, so every unit of it stays node 1 - the column is there, it just has nothing to say. Recorded rather than derived: deriving it means walking the parent chain and hard-coding which cycle closes a node, which is wrong the moment the mechanism changes, and wrong without an error.

columns.name: status
columns._: Terminal status: reached / dead_failed / dead_below_bar. Fixed once written, never revised; empty = still running

templates._: Agent context tables: one per agent in the agent table.

columns.name: task
columns._: -> task.id. Empty for an instance a user registered but has not assigned work to yet; anything unregistered does not count as existing

templates._: Agent message tables, expanded from the context table. They hold the full context, not only the half that gets pushed out.

columns.name: thought
columns._: What the model thought before it spoke (reasoning_content). It lives here and deliberately NOT in body, because body is what gets replayed: some gateways refuse an assistant message that carries reasoning back, and the replay path has always worked. Recording it costs that path nothing and buys the only account of how an answer was arrived at. Empty for any row no thinking model produced.

columns.name: prompt_tokens
columns._: Tokens sent, TOTALLED over every round this row took. A cut-off answer is continued by asking again with what was said so far, and each round bills its own prompt - so on a continued row this is the sum, not the length of any one prompt. Read it as what the input cost, never as how long the context was: one measured row billed 17232 against a conversation of about 1600 tokens, and a later row can come in lower than an earlier one simply because it was not continued. Null on any row that did not come from a model call.

columns.name: completion_tokens
columns._: Every token the model produced. This INCLUDES the thinking - reasoning_tokens is a part of this number, not a second number to add to it. Subtract to get what was actually spoken.

columns.name: reasoning_tokens
columns._: How much of completion_tokens was thinking. This is the column that says where the wall-clock went. One run averaged 174s per model call while the text that came back averaged some 350 tokens - two tokens a second, which no model is; the gap was thinking, and with no column for it that could only be inferred, never shown. A run that cannot say what it spent cannot say whether its time limit was fair.

columns.name: cached_tokens
columns._: How many of prompt_tokens the vendor served from its own cache. Kept apart from prompt_tokens because the two are priced differently, and a bill nobody can reconstruct is a bill nobody can dispute.
